overall: The AG found the Board violated the law by not taking roll call votes at its January 15 meeting with a remote member and by failing to timely approve the November 20 and December 18, 2018 minutes; remote executive session statement and January 2 minutes were not violations.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged votes at the January 15 meeting were not taken by roll call although one member participated remotely.
allegations.key_passage: The Board acknowledged that the votes were not roll call votes and we, thus, find that the Board violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged a remote member did not announce before executive session that no other person was present or able to hear the discussion.
allegations.key_passage: As such, we find that the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law when Mr. Hill failed to state in open session that no other person was present or able to hear the executive session discussions.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board failed to timely approve open session minutes of November 20, 2018, December 18, 2018, and January 2, 2018 meetings.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to approve its November 20, 2018, meeting minutes by December 20, 2018; and by failing to approve its December 18, 2018, meeting minutes by January 17.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the January 2, 2018 meeting minutes were not timely approved.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the Board timely approved its January 2 meeting minutes during its January 29 meeting and thus did not violate the Open Meeting Law as to those minutes.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law's requirements.
Approve the November 20, 2018, and December 18, 2018, meeting minutes at its next meeting.
remedy_passage: We further order the Board to approve the November 20, 2018, and December 18, 2018, meeting minutes at its next meeting.
